title: Tenant-aware telemetry governance playbook and scrub adapter framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a reusable scrub adapter framework + playbook for tenant-aware telemetry governance across tracing hooks, metrics/log pipelines, and dashboarding. Deliverables: (1) a lightweight adapter API used by collectors/ingesters to apply tenant policies, (2) default rule sets (mask, hash, drop) and a safe mode for canary rollouts, (3) retention enforcement hooks for pipelines, and (4) RBAC + immutable access logging for observability datasets. Goal is to reduce PII leakage risk while keeping <10% median tail latency increase on ingest and preserving signal for latency/error dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter API v1 defined and documented in Confluence with examples for logs/traces/metrics
Two adapter implementations: regex-based scrubber and tokenized field-hash scrubber (configurable per-tenant)
Pipeline retention enforcement implemented in metrics/log-ingest pipeline and validated with synthetic tenants
Dashboard queries automatically respect retention/field-scrub policies and show masked fields when appropriate
Access to raw observability payloads requires RBAC grant; every access emits an immutable audit record to the audit stream
Performance regression <10% p95 ingest latency in our staging cluster; memory overhead per collector <25MB
tasks: Design adapter API and configuration schema (owner: Liam)
Implement regex scrub adapter with streaming support (owner: Nora)
Implement token-hash adapter for high-sensitivity tenants (owner: Marco)
Integrate adapter hooks into trace collector and log ingest pipeline (owner: SRE team)
Add retention enforcement and TTL tags into metrics ingestion flow (owner: Telemetry infra)
Create RBAC rules and audit emitters for observability dataset access (owner: Security)
E2E tests: tenant policy matrix + performance benchmarks (owner: Eng QE)
Confluence playbook and runbook for incident response and policy changes (owner: Aisha)
notes: We must avoid global schema changes in telemetry to limit rollout blast radius; adapter should be opt-in per-collector.
Trade-off: regex scrubbing is fast but brittle; token-hash reduces false positives at cost of slight CPU and a deterministic salt management requirement.
Retention enforcement will tag metrics with retention_class to allow downstream compaction rather than immediate deletion for safety.
Plan to expose a read-only scrub-preview mode for Debug role so engineers can validate masking before policy enforcement.
This ticket intentionally scopes out ML-based PII detection (future work) to reduce complexity for the initial ship.

decisions: Scope v1 to two deterministic adapters: regex and token-hash. ML detection moved to roadmap.
Adapters run in collector pipeline as filter steps to preserve trace context and sampling behavior.
Retention classes implemented as 4 buckets (ephemeral-7d, short-30d, standard-90d, compliant-7y) to support regulatory needs.
Audit log stream will be write-once, encrypted-at-rest, and accessible only to roles with explicit audit_read permission.
risks: False positives from aggressive scrubbing could remove fields used in error-rate aggregations.
Performance regressions under high-cardinality tenants leading to higher CPU and memory usage in collectors.
Policy misconfiguration could unintentionally expose raw fields if RBAC rules are incomplete.
KMS integration delay (ENG-68311) could block token-hash rollout for regulated tenants.
